title: Spaghetti Carbonara
intro: A Roman pasta where egg, pecorino and rendered guanciale fat come together into a silky coating without any cream.
ingredients: 150 g (5 oz) guanciale or pancetta, cut into short strips
60 g (⅔ cup) pecorino romano, finely grated, plus extra to serve
steps: Bring a large pot of generously salted water to the boil and cook the spaghetti until just al dente, usually 9 to 11 minutes depending on the packet.

While the pasta cooks, put the guanciale in a wide cold frying pan and set it over medium heat so the fat renders slowly; cook for 8 to 10 minutes until the pieces are golden and crisp at the edges, then turn off the heat.
In a bowl, whisk the yolks, the whole egg, both cheeses and the black pepper into a thick paste.
Scoop out a mug of the starchy pasta water, then drain the spaghetti and tip it straight into the pan with the guanciale, tossing so every strand is coated in fat.

With the pan off the heat, pour in the egg mixture and toss quickly and continuously, adding splashes of the reserved water until the sauce turns glossy and clings to the pasta rather than scrambling.
Serve at once with extra pecorino and more black pepper over the top.

title: Lasagne
intro: Layers of pasta sheets, slow-cooked meat ragù and white sauce baked until bubbling and golden on top.
ingredients: 12 dried lasagne sheets, about 250 g (9 oz)
100 g (1 cup) parmesan, grated, plus 125 g (4½ oz) mozzarella, torn
steps: Warm the oil in a large pan and soften the onion, carrot and celery over medium heat for about 10 minutes, then stir in the garlic for a minute more.
Turn up the heat, add the mince and break it up with a spoon, cooking until it has browned all over. Pour in the wine and let it bubble away almost entirely.
Add the tinned tomatoes, tomato purée and oregano, season, and simmer gently with the lid ajar for about 1 hour, stirring now and then, until the ragù is thick.

For the white sauce, melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the milk. Keep stirring until it thickens to a pouring consistency, about 5 minutes, and season with salt, pepper and nutmeg.

Heat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). In a roughly 23 × 33 cm (9 × 13 in) baking dish, spread a thin layer of ragù, then add a layer of pasta sheets, more ragù, a ladle of white sauce and a scattering of parmesan.
Repeat the layers until everything is used, finishing with white sauce, the remaining parmesan and the mozzarella on top.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until the top is golden and the edges are bubbling, then rest for 10 minutes before cutting so the layers hold together.

title: Pizza Margherita
intro: The Neapolitan classic of a thin, blistered base with crushed tomato, melting mozzarella and fresh basil.
ingredients: 500 g (4 cups) strong white bread flour, plus extra for dusting
2 tbsp olive oil, plus extra for drizzling
400 g (14 oz) tin whole plum tomatoes
250 g (9 oz) fresh mozzarella, torn and drained
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, salt and sugar in a large bowl, then pour in the water and oil and bring everything together into a shaggy dough.
Knead on a lightly floured surface for about 10 minutes until smooth and springy, then put it in an oiled bowl, cover and leave somewhere warm for 1 to 1½ hours until doubled in size.
Meanwhile crush the tomatoes with your hands or a fork, stir in the garlic, a pinch of salt and a drizzle of oil, and set aside; it does not need cooking.
Put a pizza stone or heavy baking tray in the oven and heat it to its highest setting, 250 °C (480 °F) or above, for at least 30 minutes.
Knock the air out of the dough, divide it in two and stretch each piece on a floured surface into a thin round about 28 cm (11 in) across, keeping a slightly thicker rim.
Lay one base on floured baking paper, spread over half the tomato leaving the rim bare, dot with half the mozzarella and slide it onto the hot stone.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes until the crust is puffed and spotted with char and the cheese is bubbling, then top with basil and a drizzle of oil. Repeat with the second pizza.

title: Mushroom Risotto
intro: A creamy stirred rice dish built on dried porcini stock and finished with butter and parmesan.
ingredients: 300 g (1½ cups) arborio or carnaroli rice
steps: Soak the porcini in a mugful of the hot stock for 15 minutes, then lift them out, chop them and strain the soaking liquid back into the stock. Keep the stock at a gentle simmer on a back burner.
Heat the oil and half the butter in a wide pan and fry the fresh mushrooms over high heat until golden, about 6 minutes. Season and set aside.
In the same pan, soften the onion over medium heat for 8 minutes, add the garlic and chopped porcini for a minute, then stir in the rice and toast it for 2 minutes until the grains look glossy.
Pour in the wine and stir until it has been absorbed, then add a ladle of hot stock and stir until the rice soaks it up before adding the next.
Continue adding stock a ladle at a time, stirring often, for about 18 to 20 minutes until the rice is tender with a slight bite and the texture is loose and creamy.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the fried mushrooms, the remaining butter and the parmesan, cover and rest for 2 minutes. Season, scatter with parsley and serve.

title: Pesto Pasta
intro: Fresh basil, pine nuts, garlic and parmesan blended into a bright green sauce and tossed through hot pasta.
ingredients: 400 g (14 oz) trofie, fusilli or linguine
60 g (2 large handfuls) fresh basil leaves
50 g (½ cup) parmesan, finely grated, plus extra to serve
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil and cook the pasta according to the packet until al dente, keeping back a mug of the cooking water before draining.
While the pasta cooks, toast the pine nuts in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, shaking the pan, until lightly golden.
Put the basil, pine nuts, garlic and parmesan in a food processor and pulse to a coarse paste, then drizzle in the oil with the motor running until the pesto is loose but still textured.
Season the pesto with salt, pepper and a little lemon juice to lift the flavour.
Return the drained pasta to the pot, add the pesto and a splash of reserved water, and toss off the heat until every piece is coated and glossy. Serve with more parmesan.

title: Spaghetti Bolognese
intro: A slow-simmered beef and tomato ragù served over spaghetti, the version that became a British weeknight staple.
ingredients: 1 tsp dried oregano and 1 bay leaf
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat and cook the onion, carrot and celery with a pinch of salt for about 10 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for a minute.
Add the mince, raise the heat and fry, breaking it up, until it is browned and any liquid has cooked off.
Pour in the wine and let it reduce by half, then add the tomatoes, tomato purée, stock, oregano and bay leaf and season well.
Bring to a simmer, partly cover and cook gently for 1 hour, stirring occasionally and adding a splash of water if it looks dry, until rich and thick.
Near the end, cook the spaghetti in plenty of salted boiling water until al dente, then drain and toss with a little of the sauce.
Serve the pasta with the rest of the ragù spooned over and plenty of grated parmesan.

title: Beef Bourguignon
intro: A Burgundian stew of beef cooked slowly in red wine with bacon, small onions and mushrooms.
ingredients: 1.5 kg (3 lb 5 oz) beef chuck or shin, cut into 5 cm (2 in) chunks
2 bay leaves and 3 sprigs of thyme
300 g (10½ oz) small shallots or pearl onions, peeled
steps: Heat the oven to 160 °C (325 °F). Pat the beef dry and season it. In a large casserole, fry the lardons in the oil until golden, then lift them out.
Brown the beef in batches in the same fat over high heat, giving each piece a deep crust, and set it aside with the bacon.
Lower the heat, soften the chopped onion and carrots for 5 minutes, add the garlic, then return the meat and bacon and sprinkle over the flour, stirring for a minute.
Pour in the wine and stock, add the tomato purée, bay and thyme and bring to a simmer, scraping up anything stuck to the bottom.
Cover and transfer to the oven for 2½ to 3 hours, until the beef is tender enough to cut with a spoon.
About 20 minutes before the end, melt the butter in a frying pan and cook the shallots until golden, then add the mushrooms and fry until browned.
Stir the shallots and mushrooms into the stew, check the seasoning, and simmer uncovered on the hob for a few minutes if the sauce needs thickening.

title: Ratatouille
intro: A Provençal stew of summer vegetables, each fried separately then gently simmered together with tomato and herbs.
ingredients: 1 large aubergine, cut into 2 cm (¾ in) cubes
1 red pepper and 1 yellow pepper, cut into chunks
6 ripe tomatoes, chopped, or 400 g (14 oz) tin chopped tomatoes
2 sprigs of thyme and 1 bay leaf
steps: Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a large frying pan and fry the aubergine over medium-high heat until golden and softened, about 8 minutes, then transfer to a bowl.
Fry the courgettes in another tablespoon of oil until lightly browned, then the peppers for 5 minutes, adding each to the bowl as it is done.
In a wide casserole, cook the onion in the remaining oil over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for a minute.
Add the tomatoes, thyme and bay, season, and simmer for 10 minutes until the tomatoes start to break down.
Return all the fried vegetables to the pan, stir gently, and simmer uncovered for 25 to 30 minutes, until everything is tender and the juices have thickened but the pieces still hold their shape.
Remove the bay leaf, stir in the basil and check the seasoning. Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Coq au Vin
intro: Chicken pieces braised in red wine with bacon, mushrooms and baby onions until the sauce is dark and glossy.
ingredients: 8 chicken thighs and drumsticks, skin on, about 1.5 kg (3 lb 5 oz)
250 g (9 oz) small shallots or pearl onions, peeled
250 g (9 oz) button mushrooms, halved if large
2 bay leaves and a few sprigs of thyme
steps: Season the chicken. In a large casserole, fry the lardons in the oil until crisp and remove them, then brown the chicken pieces skin side down in the fat for about 5 minutes per side and set aside.
Add the shallots to the pan and cook until golden, then add the mushrooms and fry for 4 minutes before adding the garlic. Lift everything out onto the plate with the bacon.
Stir the flour into the remaining fat for a minute, then gradually pour in the wine and stock, whisking so no lumps form. Add the tomato purée, bay and thyme.
Return the chicken and bacon to the pan, bring to a simmer, cover and cook gently for 45 minutes.
Add the shallots and mushrooms and cook uncovered for a further 20 to 30 minutes, until the chicken is falling off the bone and the sauce has reduced.
If the sauce is still thin, lift out the chicken and boil the liquid for a few minutes, then swirl in the butter, season, and serve scattered with parsley.

title: French Onion Soup
intro: Deeply caramelised onions in beef broth, topped with toasted bread and a bubbling cap of melted Gruyère.
ingredients: 1 kg (2 lb 4 oz) onions, about 6 large, thinly sliced
2 sprigs of thyme and 1 bay leaf
steps: Melt the butter with the oil in a large heavy pan, add the onions and a pinch of salt, and cook over low-medium heat, stirring every few minutes, for 40 to 45 minutes until they are soft, sticky and a deep golden brown. Add the sugar in the last 10 minutes to help them colour.
Stir in the garlic and flour and cook for a minute, then pour in the wine and let it bubble until almost gone.
Add the stock, thyme and bay leaf, bring to a simmer and cook gently for 20 minutes. Season to taste and discard the herbs.
Heat the grill (broiler) to high and toast the baguette slices on both sides.
Ladle the soup into four ovenproof bowls, float two slices of toast on each and pile the Gruyère on top.
Put the bowls on a tray under the grill for 3 to 5 minutes, until the cheese is melted, bubbling and browned in patches. Serve immediately.

title: Seafood Paella
intro: Saffron rice cooked in a wide pan with prawns, mussels and squid, with a crisp layer at the bottom.
ingredients: 1.2 litres (5 cups) fish or chicken stock
400 g (2 cups) Spanish short-grain rice such as bomba
250 g (9 oz) squid, cleaned and sliced into rings
Lemon wedges and chopped parsley, to serve
steps: Warm the stock in a saucepan with the saffron and keep it hot.

Heat the oil in a 35 to 40 cm (14 to 16 in) paella pan or very wide frying pan over medium heat, and cook the onion and pepper for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, grated tomato and paprika and cook for 5 more minutes until thick.
Stir in the squid for a minute, then add the rice and stir to coat it in the sofrito.
Pour in the hot stock, spread the rice evenly, and bring to a brisk simmer. From now on do not stir.
Cook over medium heat for 10 minutes, then arrange the prawns and mussels on top, hinge-side down, scatter over the peas and lower the heat.
Cook for a further 8 to 10 minutes until the liquid has been absorbed, the mussels have opened and the rice is tender. Raise the heat for the last minute to form a crust underneath.
Cover the pan with a clean cloth and rest for 5 minutes, discard any unopened mussels, then serve with lemon and parsley.

title: Spanish Tortilla
intro: A thick potato and onion omelette, cooked slowly so the centre stays soft and the outside turns golden.
ingredients: 600 g (1 lb 5 oz) waxy potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
steps: Heat the oil in a 24 cm (9½ in) non-stick frying pan over medium-low heat, add the potatoes and onion with a pinch of salt and cook gently for 20 to 25 minutes, turning occasionally, until the potatoes are tender but not browned.
Drain the vegetables in a colander over a bowl, keeping the oil, and let them cool for 5 minutes.
Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper in a large bowl, then fold in the warm potatoes and onion and leave for 5 minutes so the eggs soak in.

Wipe the pan, add 2 tablespoons of the reserved oil and heat over medium. Pour in the mixture, spread it out and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, shaking the pan now and then, until the edges are set and the base is golden.
Place a large plate over the pan and confidently flip the tortilla out onto it, then slide it back into the pan uncooked side down.
Cook for 3 to 4 minutes more until just set but still slightly soft in the middle. Turn out and rest for 10 minutes before slicing into wedges.

title: Gazpacho
intro: A chilled Andalusian soup of raw tomatoes, cucumber and pepper blended smooth with olive oil and vinegar.
ingredients: 1 kg (2 lb 4 oz) very ripe tomatoes, roughly chopped
50 g (2 slices) stale white bread, crusts removed
Finely diced cucumber, pepper and croutons, to serve
steps: Soak the bread in a little cold water for 5 minutes, then squeeze it out.
Put the tomatoes, cucumber, pepper, onion, garlic, bread, vinegar and salt in a blender and blend until completely smooth, working in batches if needed.
With the blender running, pour in the olive oil in a steady stream so the soup turns creamy and slightly paler.
Push the soup through a sieve for a silky texture, then taste and adjust with more salt or vinegar; it should be bright and tangy.
Chill for at least 2 hours until very cold, then serve in bowls or glasses topped with the diced vegetables and croutons.

title: Moussaka
intro: A Greek baked dish of fried aubergine and potato layered with spiced lamb and a thick béchamel topping.
ingredients: 2 large aubergines, sliced 1 cm (½ in) thick
2 large potatoes, peeled and sliced 5 mm (¼ in) thick
1 tsp ground cinnamon and 1 tsp dried oregano
80 g (¾ cup) kefalotyri or parmesan, grated
steps: Salt the aubergine slices and leave them in a colander for 30 minutes, then rinse and pat dry. Brush them and the potato slices with oil and fry in batches in a hot pan until golden on both sides, or roast at 220 °C (425 °F) for 20 minutes. Set aside.
Soften the onion in 2 tablespoons of oil over medium heat for 8 minutes, add the garlic, then the lamb, and fry until browned.
Add the wine and let it reduce, then stir in the tomatoes, tomato purée, cinnamon and oregano. Season and simmer for 30 minutes until thick and almost dry.

For the béchamel, melt the butter, stir in the flour for a minute, then whisk in the milk gradually and cook, stirring, until very thick. Off the heat, season with nutmeg, then beat in the egg yolks and half the cheese.
Heat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Line a deep 23 × 30 cm (9 × 12 in) dish with the potato slices, cover with half the aubergine, then all the lamb, then the remaining aubergine.
Pour the béchamel over the top, smooth it out and sprinkle with the remaining cheese.
Bake for 45 to 50 minutes until the top is puffed and golden brown, then leave to stand for at least 20 minutes so it cuts cleanly.

title: Greek Salad
intro: Chunky tomatoes, cucumber, onion and olives under a slab of feta, dressed simply with olive oil and oregano.
ingredients: 4 large ripe tomatoes, cut into wedges
1 cucumber, halved lengthways and thickly sliced
steps: Put the tomatoes, cucumber, pepper and onion in a wide shallow bowl and season with a little salt so the tomatoes release some juice.
Scatter over the olives and toss everything gently with the vinegar and 3 tablespoons of the oil.
Lay the whole piece of feta on top rather than crumbling it.
Drizzle the remaining oil over the cheese, sprinkle with oregano and pepper, and serve straight away with bread to mop up the dressing.

title: Falafel
intro: Crisp, herb-flecked chickpea fritters made from soaked, uncooked chickpeas for a light, fluffy inside.
ingredients: Large handful of parsley, leaves and thin stems
steps: Soak the dried chickpeas in plenty of cold water overnight, at least 12 hours, until they have doubled in size. Do not cook them. Drain and dry well.
Put the chickpeas, onion, garlic, herbs, spices and salt in a food processor and pulse until the mixture is finely ground and holds together when squeezed, but is not a smooth paste.
Stir in the baking powder and sesame seeds, cover, and chill for 30 minutes to firm up.
Shape the mixture into walnut-sized balls or slightly flattened patties, pressing firmly so they hold together.
Heat 5 cm (2 in) of oil in a deep pan to 180 °C (350 °F). Fry the falafel in batches for 3 to 4 minutes, turning once, until deep brown and crisp.
Drain on kitchen paper and serve hot in flatbread with salad, pickles and tahini sauce.

title: Hummus
intro: A smooth chickpea and tahini dip sharpened with lemon and garlic and finished with good olive oil.
ingredients: 2 × 400 g (14 oz) tins chickpeas, drained, liquid reserved
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, plus extra to serve
Paprika and chopped parsley, to serve
steps: Blend the tahini, lemon juice, garlic and salt in a food processor for a minute until it thickens and turns pale.
Add the chickpeas and cumin and blend for 2 to 3 minutes, stopping to scrape down the sides, until completely smooth.
With the motor running, add the cold water a tablespoon at a time, then the olive oil, until the hummus is light and creamy; loosen with a little chickpea liquid if it is still stiff.
Taste and adjust the salt and lemon, then spread into a shallow bowl, swirl the surface with the back of a spoon, and top with olive oil, paprika and parsley.

title: Shakshuka
intro: Eggs poached directly in a spiced pepper and tomato sauce, served in the pan with bread for scooping.
ingredients: Handful of coriander or parsley, chopped
steps: Heat the oil in a large frying pan with a lid and cook the onion and peppers over medium heat for 10 minutes until soft and starting to colour.
Add the garlic, cumin, paprika and chilli flakes and stir for a minute until fragrant.
Tip in the tomatoes and sugar, season, and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes until the sauce has thickened enough to hold a spoon trail.
Make six hollows in the sauce with the back of a spoon and crack an egg into each one.
Cover the pan and cook over low heat for 6 to 8 minutes, until the whites are set but the yolks are still runny.
Scatter with herbs and black pepper and serve straight from the pan with warm bread.

title: Chicken Shawarma
intro: Chicken thighs marinated in warm spices and lemon, roasted until charred and sliced into flatbread with garlic sauce.
ingredients: 800 g (1 lb 12 oz) boneless skinless chicken thighs
½ tsp ground cinnamon and ½ tsp ground allspice
150 g (⅔ cup) plain yogurt mixed with 1 crushed garlic clove and a squeeze of lemon
Shredded lettuce, sliced tomato and pickled cucumbers, to serve
steps: Mix the oil, lemon juice, garlic, all the spices and the salt in a large bowl, add the chicken and turn to coat. Cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Spread the chicken in a single layer on a lined baking tray.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, turning halfway, until cooked through and charred at the edges. For extra colour, finish under a hot grill for 2 to 3 minutes.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes, then slice it thinly across the grain and toss the slices in the juices on the tray.
Warm the flatbreads, spread each with garlic yogurt, pile on the chicken, lettuce, tomato and pickles, then roll up tightly and serve.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
intro: A thin veal escalope in a wavy golden breadcrumb coat, shallow-fried in plenty of fat and served with lemon.
ingredients: 4 veal escalopes, about 150 g (5 oz) each
150 g (2 cups) fine dry white breadcrumbs
150 g (⅔ cup) clarified butter or lard, or a mix of butter and neutral oil
steps: Lay each escalope between two sheets of baking paper and pound it with a rolling pin or meat mallet to an even 4 mm (⅙ in) thickness. Season both sides.
Set out three shallow dishes: flour in the first, eggs beaten with the milk in the second, breadcrumbs in the third.
Dust a cutlet in flour, shake off the excess, dip it in the egg, then lay it in the crumbs and press lightly so they stick without compacting. Repeat with the rest.
Heat the fat in a large frying pan over medium-high heat until a crumb sizzles instantly; it should be at least 1 cm (½ in) deep.
Fry the schnitzels one or two at a time for 2 to 3 minutes per side, spooning hot fat over the top and swirling the pan so the coating puffs and ripples, until golden brown.
Drain briefly on kitchen paper and serve right away with lemon wedges and a potato or cucumber salad.

title: Beef Goulash
intro: A Hungarian stew of beef and onions coloured deep red with sweet paprika and simmered until meltingly tender.
ingredients: 1 kg (2 lb 4 oz) beef chuck, cut into 3 cm (1¼ in) cubes
500 g (1 lb 2 oz) waxy potatoes, cut into chunks
steps: Melt the lard in a large heavy pan and cook the onions over medium heat for 15 minutes until soft and golden, then add the garlic and caraway.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the paprika so it does not scorch, then add the beef and tomato purée and stir to coat the meat.
Return to the heat, add the pepper, carrots, stock and bay leaves, season, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and cook slowly for 1½ hours, stirring occasionally, until the beef is starting to become tender.
Add the potatoes and simmer uncovered for 30 to 40 minutes more until they are cooked through and the sauce has thickened. Check the seasoning and serve in bowls.

title: Potato and Cheese Pierogi
intro: Half-moon Polish dumplings filled with mashed potato and fresh cheese, boiled then pan-fried in butter with onions.
ingredients: 400 g (3¼ cups) plain flour, plus extra for dusting
500 g (1 lb 2 oz) floury potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
200 g (7 oz) twaróg or full-fat cottage cheese, drained
Salt and plenty of black pepper
steps: Mix the flour and salt, make a well and add the egg, oil and warm water. Bring together and knead for 5 to 8 minutes until smooth and soft, then wrap and rest for 30 minutes.

Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 to 20 minutes until tender, drain well and mash. Fry one of the onions in 20 g of the butter until golden and stir it into the mash with the cheese; season generously and let it cool.
Roll the dough out thinly on a floured surface to about 2 mm (just under ⅛ in) and cut out 8 cm (3 in) rounds.
Place a heaped teaspoon of filling on each round, fold it over into a half-moon and pinch the edges firmly closed, crimping so they do not open while cooking.
Cook the pierogi in batches in a large pan of gently boiling salted water; they are done 2 to 3 minutes after they float to the surface. Lift out with a slotted spoon.
Fry the second onion in the remaining butter until golden, then add the boiled pierogi and fry for a few minutes until lightly crisp on both sides. Serve with the onions and soured cream.

title: Fish and Chips
intro: White fish in a crisp beer batter with twice-cooked chips, served with salt and malt vinegar.
ingredients: 4 thick white fish fillets such as cod or haddock, about 180 g (6 oz) each, skinless
1 kg (2 lb 4 oz) floury potatoes, peeled and cut into thick chips
200 g (1⅔ cups) plain flour, plus 3 tbsp for dusting
300 ml (1¼ cups) cold lager or pale ale
Neutral oil, for deep-frying, about 2 litres (8 cups)
Malt vinegar and salt, to serve
steps: Rinse the cut chips in cold water, then simmer them in a pan of salted water for 5 to 7 minutes until just tender at the edges. Drain carefully and spread on a tray to dry and cool.
Heat the oil in a deep heavy pan or fryer to 140 °C (285 °F). Fry the chips in batches for 6 to 8 minutes until soft and pale, lift out and drain. Raise the oil to 180 °C (350 °F).
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt with the cold beer until you have a smooth batter the thickness of double cream. Use it straight away.
Pat the fish dry, dust it in the extra flour, then dip it in the batter and lower it gently into the hot oil, holding it for a few seconds so it does not stick to the bottom.
Fry two fillets at a time for 7 to 8 minutes, turning once, until the batter is deep golden and crisp. Drain on a rack.
Return the chips to the oil at 180 °C (350 °F) for 3 to 4 minutes until golden and crunchy, drain, and season. Serve with the fish, salt and vinegar.

title: Shepherd's Pie
intro: Minced lamb in rich gravy under a blanket of buttery mashed potato, baked until the top is crisp and golden.
ingredients: 400 ml (1⅔ cups) lamb or beef stock
1 tsp dried thyme and 1 bay leaf
1.2 kg (2 lb 10 oz) floury potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan and cook the onion and carrots over medium heat for 8 minutes, then add the garlic for a minute.
Add the lamb, raise the heat and fry until browned, breaking up any lumps and pouring off excess fat if there is a lot.

Stir in the tomato purée and flour for a minute, then add the Worcestershire sauce, stock, thyme and bay leaf. Simmer uncovered for 25 to 30 minutes until the gravy is thick, then stir in the peas and season.
Meanwhile boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 to 20 minutes until tender, drain and leave to steam dry for a minute, then mash with the butter and milk until smooth. Season well.
Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Spoon the lamb into a roughly 2 litre (2 quart) baking dish, remove the bay leaf, and spread the mash over the top, roughing up the surface with a fork.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the top is golden and crisp at the edges and the filling bubbles up around the sides.

title: Swedish Meatballs
intro: Small, tender beef and pork meatballs with a hint of allspice, served in a cream gravy with lingonberry jam.
ingredients: 1 small onion, very finely chopped or grated
Lingonberry jam and mashed potatoes, to serve
steps: Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk for 10 minutes. Meanwhile soften the onion in 1 tablespoon of the butter over low heat for 5 minutes and let it cool.
Mix the soaked crumbs, onion, both minces, egg, allspice, white pepper and salt together thoroughly with your hands until the mixture is smooth and sticky.
With wet hands, roll the mixture into balls about 3 cm (1¼ in) across; you should get around 30.
Melt half the remaining butter in a large frying pan over medium heat and fry the meatballs in batches for 8 to 10 minutes, turning so they brown evenly and are cooked through. Set aside.

Add the remaining butter to the pan, stir in the flour and cook for a minute, then gradually whisk in the stock until smooth. Add the cream and soy sauce and simmer for 5 minutes until the gravy coats a spoon.
Return the meatballs to the pan and warm them through in the sauce for 5 minutes. Serve with mashed potato and a spoonful of lingonberry jam.
